input.question: In the same graph-theoretic setting for a homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) and its associated graph G(P), what necessary or sufficient conditions on the labeled graph G(P) guarantee that the Vanishing Conjecture holds for the homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomial P(z)?

original_question: In the same graph-theoretic setting for a homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) and its associated graph G(P), what necessary or sufficient conditions on the labeled graph G(P) guarantee that the Vanishing Conjecture holds for the homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomial P(z)?

original_paper.title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials

rewritten_question: Let P(z) be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d at least 2. By the structural decomposition for such polynomials, write P(z) as a finite sum P(z) = Σ h_{α_i}(z)^d where each α_i is isotropic for the standard complex bilinear form, and associate to P the graph G(P) with vertex set {1, ..., k}, where vertices i and j are adjacent exactly when ⟨α_i, α_j⟩ is nonzero; one may also label each edge by the pairing ⟨α_i, α_j⟩, or when d is even by the corresponding symmetric polynomial weight used to form the matrix Ψ_{P,(d-2)/2}. Assume in addition that P is Hessian nilpotent. Determine graph-theoretic conditions, ideally stated directly in terms of the labeled graph G(P), that are sufficient or necessary for the Vanishing Conjecture to hold for P, meaning that Δ^m(P^{m+1}) = 0 for all sufficiently large m. It is already known that one may reduce to the case where G(P) is connected, and that the conjecture holds in certain special families: for example when the span of the vectors α_i has dimension 1, 2, k-1, or k, and also in the case where that span has dimension k-2 and G(P) is connected, which forces G(P) to be the complete bipartite graph K(4, k-4). The problem is to identify broader necessary or sufficient conditions on the labeled graph itself that guarantee this eventual vanishing.

resolution.status_reason: The primary paper explicitly poses this as an open problem, and a bounded later-literature search found partial graph-theoretic sufficient cases and obstructions, but no explicit later paper that states or proves a general necessary-and-sufficient graph criterion guaranteeing the Vanishing Conjecture for homogeneous Hessian nilpotent P(z).

paper_evidence.quote: A polynomial or formal power series P(z) is said to be HN (Hessian nilpotent) if its Hessian matrix Hes P := ( ∂2P/∂zi∂zj ) are nilpotent.
Conjecture 1.1. (Vanishing Conjecture) Let ∆ := Σni=1 D2i be the Laplace operator of C[z]. Then, for any HN polynomial P(z) (of homogeneous of degree d = 4), ∆mPm+1(z) = 0 when m >> 0.

Theorem 8.1. For any homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) of degree d ≥ 2, we have P(z) = Σki=1 cid hαi(z) for some ci ∈ C× and αi ∈ X(Cn) (1 ≤ i ≤ k). Note that, replacing αi in Eq. (8.1) by c−1/di αi, we may also write P(z) as P(z) = Σki=1 hdαi(z) with αi ∈ X(Cn) (1 ≤ i ≤ k).

We fix an expression as in Eq. (8.2) for P(z). The set of vertices of G(P) will be the set of positive integers [k] := {1, 2, . . . , k}. The vertices i and j of G(P) are connected by an edge iff hαi, αj i ̸= 0.

Furthermore, we may also label edges of G(P) by assigning hαi, αj i or (h(d−2)/2αi hαi, αj ih(d−2)/2αi), when d is even, for the edge connecting vertices i, j ∈ [k]. We then get a labeled graph whose adjacency matrix is exactly AP or ΨP,(d−2)/2 (depending on the labels we choose for the edges of G(P)).

Open Problem 8.4. (a) Find some necessary or sufficient conditions on the (labeled) graph G(P) such that the homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) is HN. (b) Find some necessary or sufficient conditions on the (labeled) graph G(P) such that the VC holds for the homogeneous HN polynomial P(z).
Corollary 8.5. To study homogeneous HN polynomials P or the VC for homogeneous HN polynomials P, it will be enough to consider the case when G(P) is connected.

Theorem 8.6. ([Wi]) Let P be a homogeneous HN polynomial as in Eq.(8.2) with d ≥ 4. Let l(P) be the dimension of the vector subspace of Cn spanned by {αi | 1 ≤ i ≤ k}. Then (1) If l(P) = 1, 2, k −1 or k, the graph G(P) is totally disconnected ... (2) If l(P) = k − 2 and G(P) is connected, then G(P) is the complete bi-graph K(4, k − 4). (3) In the case of (a) and (b) above, the VC holds.

The main result of this article asserts that in the case dim([α1,…,αs])≤2 or ≥s−2, the Jacobian Conjecture holds for the maps x+∇f. In fact, we give a complete description of the graphs of such f's, whose Hessian is nilpotent. As an application of the result, we show that lines and cycles cannot appear as graphs of HN polynomials.
